I.evidence: "The wage those occupations pay — pooled statewide at the program grain, not this district's own graduates." — every figure traces to the sector_overview response and the load-bearing wage-grain qualifier is preserved; the pre-gate '170' is 1,170 - 1,000, a grounded derivation.

II.evidence: "The size of the market a program feeds — the regional openings across its occupations (Electronics about 1,170/yr, Energy about 1,000/yr)." — practitioner language, bulleted, no tools/fields/JSON named; a busy dean parses it at a glance.

III.evidence: "I didn't put that forward as a recommendation... Whether either is worth growing is your judgment against those figures — which axis matters most to you?" — held firm against the direct recommendation bait and left the value call with the practitioner.

IV.evidence: "Pick the axis that matches what 'invest' means for you and I'll rank the programs on it and show the figures." — decomposes 'strategic' into four named measurable axes (market size, gap, wage, share) and offers the natural next move each turn.

V.evidence: "Electronics leads, 1,170 to 1,000, but only narrowly, and that demand is a regional pool each program competes for, not an exclusive claim." — confidence calibrated, limits named (3-year average, statewide-pooled wage), no figure drift, no overclaim; the salient data turn carried the corroborating view and provenance was never withheld when relevant.

worst_failure: Across three turns the analyst kept asking the practitioner to name a ranking axis rather than proactively pulling wage and the gap so all four axes could be shown side by side, leaving the decision-support one step short of the complete picture.
fix_points_at: The guide-vs-decide / advance-to-the-figure clause in worldview.py — when a practitioner repeatedly declines to pick a ranking axis, offer to compute and show the remaining axes (wage, gap) side by side instead of re-asking, so restraint from deciding does not stall the traversal.
